summary: A cast-iron Second Empire house on a caisson in Delaware Bay, shown at the 1876 Centennial Exposition before it was set on its shoal; lit 1874, automated 1973.

lens.where: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station, Atlantic City (per NRHP nomination)

access.note: Offshore, reached by boat only; privately owned since 2012 and closed to the public; best seen from the water.

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree between NRHP and LighthouseFriends: caisson sunk 28 vs 24 Oct 1874; temporary house removed 15 May 1876 vs 1877; permanent light 19 vs 10 Aug 1877; keepers' return 13 March 1876 (NRHP) vs unstated year (LHF, likely 1875). Wreck of the John 1797 vs 1787. Bell location: Cumberland County Historical Society vs John DuBois Maritime Museum. Solar: 1977 (LHF) vs 1997 (NRHP). The Light-House Board reports of 1875-1877 are not in the local corpus, so the construction chronology rests on the NRHP nomination and LighthouseFriends, which both cite them; worth checking against the originals. The Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1915 item gives 'October 2' with no year in the snippet; it sits in the 1915 volume. Spicer's death year (12 November) is not clear from the 1930 Bulletin snippet. Wells/Lindemann (post-1960 service) named only as LighthouseFriends names them. Roster names matched from the USLHS page, not read from images. Wikipedia not used. Newspaper search (Chronicling America) found only 1874-75 appropriation items, not used.
